summary: This plugin runs after a Docusaurus build completes and creates plain-text Markdown copies of every published blog post. It finds all blog post source files, extracts their content, strips out Docusaurus-specific markers, adds a hidden comment with metadata (like the canonical URL), and writes the result as a .md file alongside the HTML output so readers can access the raw Markdown version.

explanations.15: withFileTypes: true tells the function to return objects describing each file/folder rather than just names, so we can check whether each entry is a directory or file.
explanations.18: The three dots (...) spread operator unpacks the array returned from the recursive call, adding all nested results to the found array instead of nesting arrays inside arrays.
explanations.46: A Set is created from routesPaths to make the lookup on line 61 fast—checking if a route exists in a Set is much quicker than searching through an array.
explanations.53: frontMatter parses a string that has YAML metadata at the top (like `slug: my-post`) followed by the actual content, splitting it into attributes (the parsed YAML as an object) and body (the content below).
explanations.64: This removes the Docusaurus 'truncate' marker that tells the homepage to show only a preview, then trims whitespace and adds back a single newline at the end.
explanations.67: recursive: true ensures parent directories are created if they don't exist yet, so we don't crash when writing to a path with missing folders.
